sections.h2: Where is Trussville, Alabama, and what is it near?
sections.html:
Trussville is a suburb of Birmingham in Jefferson and St. Clair counties, and it belongs to the Birmingham-Hoover metropolitan area. The city covers about 35 square miles and sits at 709 feet of elevation.

U.S. Route 11 runs through it, and the city's shopping districts include Colonial Promenade at Trussville on the west side and the Tutwiler Farm centers along Highway 11 at the I-59 and I-459 interchange. The ZIP code is 35173.

The first European settler was Warren Truss, who arrived with his brothers in 1821 and built a grist mill on the Cahaba River. The community stayed agricultural until a railroad came through after the Civil War, and a blast furnace was running by 1886.

Trussville was incorporated as a town on June 10, 1947, and on May 31, 1957 it became a city under its current name. Its growth since then has been steep: between 1980 and 2010 the city grew by more than 500 percent.

sections.h2: What is the Cahaba Project, and why does it matter to Trussville houses?
sections.html:
The Cahaba Project was a planned neighborhood that the federal Resettlement Administration built in the 1930s. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2006.

The development included 243 single-family houses and 44 duplexes at a total cost of $2,661,981.26. Designer W. H. Kestler laid out dense streets with houses on half to three quarter acre lots around a central green called The Mall. The houses were rented to approved lower-middle-income families for $14 to $23 a month.

  • Most were one- and two-level homes in the American four-square style.
  • Materials included brick and wood siding, pine floors and metal roofs.
  • Each house had electricity, hot and cold running water and a sewer connection.

After World War II the government sold the houses to their residents. If you own a house in or near the Cahaba Project, its age and historic status may influence repairs and buyer interest, and the city or the National Park Service can explain any rules that apply.

sections.h2: What was daily life like in the Cahaba Project, and what is left of it?
sections.html:
Planners first imagined the Cahaba Project as a rural community of small farmsteads, then moved it near Birmingham so residents could commute by public transit. About 60 existing houses were demolished to make room, and the design was approved in 1936 and built over the following two years.

The village had its own pool, an elementary school and a high school, a co-op store that doubled as a lending library, and a communal washer building on The Mall. Many residents planted Victory Gardens during World War II. African American families were housed in cottages on a 40-acre tract known as Washington Heights, or more commonly The Forties.

The project also produced friction. Wikipedia notes resentment between its residents and families in "Old Trussville," many of whom lacked electricity and indoor plumbing at the time. The project is now listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

sections.h2: How many people live in Trussville?
sections.html:
Trussville had 26,123 residents at the 2020 census and a Census Bureau estimate of 27,273 for 2025. The population has grown through every census since 1950.

The 2020 census counted 9,173 households and 9,492 housing units, of which 3.4 percent were vacant. The rental vacancy rate was 9.4 percent and the homeowner vacancy rate was 1.3 percent.

sections.h2: What is the Trussville household profile?
sections.html:
The median age in Trussville was 40.1 years in 2020, and 26.1 percent of residents were under 18. Married couples made up 69.1 percent of households, and 40.8 percent of households had children under 18.

About 16.9 percent of households were one person living alone. Roughly 78 percent of residents lived in urban areas and 22 percent in rural areas, so parts of the city are still semi-rural.

sections.h2: What do Trussville residents do for work?
sections.html:
An older economic snapshot cited by Wikipedia (2014 data) put the median family income at $94,875, with 1.1 percent of families below the poverty line. The same snapshot said sales and administration jobs accounted for 28 percent of positions, management, business and finance for 24 percent, healthcare for 9 percent and education for 8 percent.

These figures are dated, and the Census Bureau's current data are the better guide. If a job move is behind your sale, plan the closing date around it.

Trussville City Schools serve 4,269 students. The system was part of Jefferson County Schools until 2005, when it separated after a county financial crisis in 2000 forced cuts to teacher funding and the city could not offset them with its own money. The city council created the Trussville Board of Education in 2004.

The system has five schools:

  • Hewitt-Trussville High School, grades 9 to 12
  • Hewitt-Trussville Middle School, grades 6 to 8
  • Cahaba Elementary School, grades K to 5
  • Magnolia Elementary School, grades K to 5
  • Paine Elementary School, grades K to 5

The Trussville Tribune, published weekly, covers local news.

sections.h2: What do Trussville sellers face on the market side?
sections.html:
A seller's main challenge is reaching buyers in a strong family suburb who expect a move-in-ready house. When a house needs work, a conventional listing can mean repairs, showings and weeks of waiting.

A direct sale to a cash buyer avoids repairs and financing conditions, but you should weigh the offer against what a repaired listing would bring after costs.

sections.h2: What taxes and recording steps apply to a Trussville sale?
sections.html:
Alabama property tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, per the Alabama Department of Revenue. Because Trussville lies in two counties, ask whichever county office bills your parcel for the exact balance. Clair County tax page.

The recordation tax under Alabama Code section 40-22-1 is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction. The statute lets the tax apply only to value above any mortgage on which the mortgage tax was paid, and it splits the proceeds two thirds to the state and one third to the county. Your closing agent will calculate the final figure.

  • Order a title search early.
  • Pay off liens and any unpaid taxes at closing.
  • Bring proof of the purchase price to the recording office.

sections.h2: When is a cash sale a fit in Trussville?
sections.html:
A cash sale fits when you would rather skip repairs and showings. Common Trussville examples include:

  • An older Cahaba Project house that needs updating.
  • An inherited house that family members want to sell quickly.
  • A rental with a tenant situation you want to end.
  • A house with deferred roof, plumbing or foundation work.

We buy Trussville houses as they are. You can request an offer and decide whether it fits.
